summary: SCIM email-alias rewrite left bastion SSH access approval requests orphaned
description: Several recent internal access requests for SSH bastion access stalled in the approval queue after a mass SCIM attribute normalization job rewrote primary email aliases. Users report their approval requests show as 'Pending' but never progress to the approver UI; onboarding engineers cannot assume roles via the bastion runbook. The issue appeared immediately after the SCIM downstream sync (email alias rewrite) completed for ~120 accounts.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a SCIM sync that rewrites primary email alias (example: user@old -> user@new) via identity-provisioner job
Submit a new bastion SSH access request for an affected user through the internal console
Observe that request appears in the approval-queue with status 'Pending' but approvers do not receive UI notification or webhook
Attempt to manually approve via support console: approval action returns 200 but request status remains 'Pending'
Check approval-queue service logs for 'orphaned-request' markers and SCIM user id mismatches
logs_and_observations: 2026-03-01T07:12:23Z approval-queue INFO Request created id=aq_0b9c user_id=usr_82f (old_email=user@old)
2026-03-01T07:12:40Z scim-provisioner INFO Rewrote primary_email for usr_82f old=user@old new=user@new
2026-03-01T07:13:01Z approval-queue WARN Approver webhook failed 404 for approver_id=appr_11 (lookup by email returned no user)
Support console: manual approve POST /approve returned 200 but internal state transition did not occur (no state_change event emitted)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SCIM rewrite changed canonical email used as foreign key in approval-queue; approver lookup uses stale email index
Observed race: request creation timestamp sits between SCIM rewrite operations for same user; approval-queue relies on email-based join rather than immutable user_id
Temporary mitigation validated: re-running identity cache refresh for affected user allowed approver webhook to resolve user and advance status
Root cause appears to be non-atomic update between scim-provisioner and identity-cache invalidation; approval-queue did not listen for scim events to reconcile pending requests
comments: Priya Nair 2026-03-01: Customer (internal) pinged #support — several new hires blocked from bastion SSH; observed after identity provisioning job. Creating ticket and triaging.

Diego Ramirez 2026-03-01: I reproduced locally in staging by reordering events. Approval-queue is keyed by primary_email; switching to immutable user_id would prevent this. Adding identity-provisioner and approval-queue owners to thread.

SRE Lead (Samir Patel) 2026-03-02: Confirmed state-change event failed to emit because approval-queue consumer index returned empty for approver lookup. Recommend hotfix: invalidate email index after SCIM sync and process pending queue reconciliation job.

Diego Ramirez 2026-03-03: Hotfix branch created: identity-provisioner#fix/scim-email-index-reconcile (PR queued). Canary deploy planned for 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC. Will run reconciliation to advance orphaned requests.
Priya Nair 2026-03-03: Noted ~12 high-priority onboarding requests affected. Communicated manual workaround to People Ops to re-run provisioning for those accounts.
workaround: Run ad-hoc identity-cache refresh for affected user_id via support CLI: `redwood-identity cache:refresh --user usr_82f`
If cache refresh not possible, manually map approver to request via internal support console admin action 'force-approve' (requires SRE approval)
resolution: Pending - hotfix branch created and canary scheduled. Post-canary reconciliation job will update orphaned approvals. Final resolution will include switching approval-queue joins to immutable user_id and adding SCIM post-sync cache invalidation
